Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope the technical deep-dive:

High-level notes from the call:
- Primary product: customer-facing chat UI (real-time) + background batch summarization pipelines.
- Expected max context: ~8k tokens on average, spikes to ~12k for enterprise support threads.
- Will use semantic search (embeddings) + reranker for candidate selection, plus a small set of tool calls (product_lookup, account_lookup).

Questions / areas we called out for the deep-dive:
1) SDK & auth: are you planning to use API keys from the hosted Redwood API, or run a Private deployment (VPC) with service-account style credentials? DevOps had some questions about token rotation and audit logs.
2) Routing & model variants: do you anticipate routing by region/tier (e.g., EU vs US) or by latency vs cost (gptx-lowlat vs gptx-eco)?
3) Structured output / tool calling: will you rely on forced JSON outputs, or prefer Redwood's function/tool calling flow? We discussed tradeoffs for deterministic parsing vs streaming.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: expected batch sizes, and whether you want Redwood-managed embedding compute or to run embedding generation in your infra.
5) Request/response schema specifics: chat vs completions payloads, tokenization impact on max_tokens, stop sequences behavior, and streaming semantics (partial chunks/deltas).

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep-dive (Ben + Jonas) to go over SDK snippets, auth options, and function-calling examples.
- Share a short proposal and SDK snippets (attached) with recommended defaults for your use case.
- If you can share a representative example message (sanitized) or expected traffic profile that will help us make concrete batching/quantization recommendations.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Thursday 6/18 10:00 AM PT or Friday 6/19 2:00 PM PT — let me know what works.

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A few quick answers from our side to help scope the deep-dive:

- Auth: We prefer hosted API keys for initial PoC (easier), but Enterprise teams will likely require a VPC/private deployment with service-account credentials. DevOps will follow up with specific rotation/audit requirements.
- Routing/model variants: We'll start with a single region (US) and prefer a low-latency variant for chat. For batch jobs we can use a cost-optimized model. So routing by workload type is what we want.
- Structured output/tool calling: We want function/tool calling for the product_lookup flow (deterministic), but still need fallback plain-text generation for exploratory features.
- Embeddings/rerankers: We'll run embedding generation in our infra initially (we have existing embedding infra), but would like best practices for batching and reranking.

Two specific technical questions before the deep-dive:
1) Streaming semantics: in the Redwood API, when streaming chat responses, do we get incremental function-call arguments (i.e., can a function call stream name+partial args), or are function-call args only delivered at the final chunk? We need low-latency partial content for UI while still supporting tool-calls.
2) max_tokens / tokenization: For chat payloads, does max_tokens apply per-choice, and how does tokenization count across role/name framing (messages array)? If we set max_tokens to 512 and our prompt+context is 7,500 tokens against a 8k model, will we get a failure or will the runtime truncate?

If you can include those clarifications in the deep-dive, that would be great.

Jordan

Subject: Re: Acme - integration follow-up: RSP schema / chat vs completions questions

Jordan — thanks for the great questions. Quick technical clarifications to help prep the deep-dive (high-level, we can share SDK snippets in the call):

1) Chat vs Completions (payload & tokens)
- Chat: you send an array of messages (role/name/content). On the wire we serialize messages for token counting. Tokens are computed from the serialized representation, including role/name framing.
- Completions: single prompt string (classic).
- max_tokens: controls the maximum number of generated tokens (the completion). Redwood enforces that prompt_tokens + max_tokens must be <= model_context_window. If the combined size exceeds the model's context window, the request will return a 4xx error indicating context length exceeded — we do not silently truncate user prompt. For streaming and UX we recommend checking token counts client-side (SDK helpers) before sending.

2) Stop sequences
- Supported for both completions and chat. For chat, stop sequences are matched against the generated output stream. If you rely on strict delimiter-based termination for structured JSON, we generally recommend function/tool calling (or explicit end tokens) because stop sequences can be brittle across tokenizers and streaming.

3) Streaming semantics & function calls
- Streaming returns incremental delta chunks for content. For function/tool calling in streaming mode, Redwood will stream the function call as a series of "argument" deltas and a finalizer event with the completed JSON object. That means your UI can render partial text while the function arguments are still being streamed. However, some SDKs buffer function args until a closing chunk — plan your client accordingly.

4) Embeddings & rerankers
- Embeddings are a separate API. Recommended pattern: compute embeddings for candidates, compute query embedding, score via cosine distance, and then rerank. For production, we recommend batching at 256-1024 vectors per request depending on your GPU/CPU throughput; also consider caching embeddings for stable content.

5) Routing & batching suggestions
- For chat real-time: use small batch sizes and lower-latency instances. For batch summarization and reranking: larger batches and quantized models to save cost. We can provide quantization recommendations once we see sample traffic.
